newsitem.title: CHILE: Castro visits Allende's tomb in Chile.
newsitem.headline: Castro visits Allende's tomb in Chile.

text.p: Cuban President Fidel Castro visited the tomb of Chile's late socialist president Salvador Allende on Sunday in a quiet, emotional homage.
He visited the tomb the day after General Augusto Pinochet, who ousted Allende in a 1973 coup and ruled Chile for 17 years, appeared to compare the Cuban leader to the devil.

Castro, who arrived on Saturday for his first visit to Chile since Allende's tumultuous presidency in 1971, stood for a few moments at the stone tomb emblazoned with Allende's name at Santiago's General Cemetery.
Wearing a blue civilian suit, Castro also greeted Allende's daughter Isabel and Chilean leftist politicians in the early-morning visit amid crowds of reporters and bodyguards.

A hush fell over the scene as Castro climbed the few stairs to the tomb of Allende, who was elected in 1970 and presided over Chile for three turbulent years until he was overthrown in a military coup.

Allende died in the coup as military planes bombed the presidential palace. His personal physician later said he saw Allende commit suicide with a submachine gun given to him by Castro, but some ex-confidants say he was murdered.
He visited the tomb about an hour before the opening of the sixth Ibero-American Summit of leaders from 19 Latin American nations plus Spain and Portugal at a Santiago convention centre.

Castro's visit has revived memories of the Allende years and sparked controversy in Chile, though street rallies called by Cuban exiles and local rightists against his regime have fizzled out. One demonstration on Saturday drew no more than 150 people.
Pinochet, who led the 1973 coup and is still army commander-in-chief, said late on Saturday that if he were in Santiago for the summit, he would greet Castro if ordered to by President Eduardo Frei.

"If tomorrow the government wants to invite Lucifer and Lucifer comes here, what am I going to do if I my orders come from the government?" said Pinochet in a television interview Saturday night from the northern city fo Iquique.
"I consider (Castro's visit) just another visit, nothing more," said Pinochet. "I have no interest in confronting Fidel Castro."
Pinochet was attending military exercises in northern Chile with the leaders of the Chilean air force and navy.
